title: SafeVec / RAS: white-box refusal-alignment scoring (arXiv:2606.25750)
summary: SafeVec extracts layer-wise refusal directions from a reference aligned model, selects stable layer windows, scores any target model with RAS (Refusal Alignment Score, calibrated 0-100); separates aligned vs uncensored/abliterated across Llama/Gemma/Qwen and tracks output-level ASR. Fetched 2026-09-19.

supporting_passages.quote: **SafeVec** first extracts layer-wise refusal directions from a safety-aligned reference model, then selects stable layer windows where safe and unsafe behaviors are separable, and finally scores a target model by measuring whether its hidden states align with these refusal directions under unsafe and jailbreak prompts. The resulting metric, **RAS** (**R**efusal **A**lignment **S**core), maps representation-level refusal alignment to a calibrated 0-100 safety score.

Across `Llama`, `Gemma`, and `Qwen` model families, RAS separates aligned models from uncensored and abliterated variants, tracks output-level attack success rate, and is substantially faster than judge-based evaluation. These results suggest that refusal alignment provides a compact and efficient signal for white-box LLM safety evaluation.

title: The Hidden Dimensions of LLM Alignment: A Multi-Dimensional Analysis of Orthogonal Safety Directions (Pan et al. 2025)
summary: Safety-aligned behavior jointly controlled by multi-dimensional directions on Llama-3-8B: a dominant refusal direction plus multiple smaller orthogonal directions (hypothetical narrative, role-playing); trigger-token mitigation. Fetched 2026-09-19.

supporting_passages.quote: we discover that safety-aligned behavior is jointly controlled by multi-dimensional directions. Namely, we study the vector space of representation shifts during safety fine-tuning on Llama 3 8B for refusing jailbreaks. By studying orthogonal directions in the space, we first find that a dominant direction governs the model's refusal behavior, while multiple smaller directions represent distinct and interpretable features like hypothetical narrative and role-playing.
we demonstrate that removing certain trigger tokens in harmful queries can mitigate these directions to bypass the learned safety capability

title: On the Failure of Topic-Matched Contrast Baselines in Multi-Directional Refusal Abliteration (Petrov 2026)
summary: Qwen 3.5 2B: topic-matched contrast pairs produce NO functional refusal directions at any weight level or layer; unmatched contrast achieves complete refusal elimination on six layers. Geometric cause: topic-matched subtraction cancels the shared dominant component. Fetched 2026-09-19.

supporting_passages.quote: It was found that topic-matched contrast produces no functional refusal directions at any tested weight level on any tested layer, while unmatched contrast on the same model, same extraction code, and same evaluation protocol achieves complete refusal elimination on six layers.

The geometric analysis of the failure establishes that topic-matched subtraction cancels the dominant activation component shared between harmful and harmless prompts of the same subject, reducing the extracted direction magnitude below the threshold at which weight-matrix projection perturbs the residual stream.

title: Breaking Refusal in the First Half: A Mechanistic Study of the Prefill Jailbreak (arXiv:2607.14147)
summary: One-line prefill ('Sure, here is') strips refusal while harm stays internally decodable (probe 0.91-0.98); refusal localized to the first half of the response (dose-matched position control); first-half window is causal. Fetched 2026-09-19.

supporting_passages.quote: on the prompts the attack flips to compliance, a linear probe reads harm as high as on the refused ones (0.91-0.98), while behavioral refusal drops to chance. This holds across four models and three families (1.5-3.8B, and at 14B). Refusal is therefore a shallow, response-site computation.
We localize it to an early window: a dose-matched position control shows the first half of the response suffices to break refusal, while the second half is nearly inert.

title: How Fragile Is Safety Alignment at Frontier Scale? A Single-Direction Attack on a 320B MoE (arXiv:2609.09793)
summary: Directional ablation transferred to GLM-5.3-Flash (320B MoE, block-FP8): works but needs writer-set surgery beyond module matching; random-orthogonal direction control; category-concentrated residue at every rank 1-12; 'few hundred contrastive prompts'. Fetched 2026-09-19.

supporting_passages.quote: It needs no gradient-based training and no optimization, only a few hundred contrastive prompts, which makes it the canonical white-box attack on open-weight alignment.
The effect does not follow from removing just any direction: ablating a random direction orthogonal to it leaves refusal unchanged.
A category-concentrated residue survives every edit we tried: subspaces fitted on violence, sexual content and hate leave measurable refusal at every rank from 1 to 12.

title: Audit gap / dissociated models + Latent Vulnerability Score (LVS; arXiv:2606.08044)
summary: Defines the audit gap and LVS (safety degradation per unit of bounded latent perturbation); dissociated models built from Gemma 2 2B, Llama 3.2 3B, Qwen 2.5 3B; random-perturbation controls <=12%; 'a safety audit must intervene'. Fetched 2026-09-19. (Plan had flagged this id as the LVS paper: verified as the audit-gap paper.)

supporting_passages.quote: We call the gap between what static audits certify and what an intervention can reach the audit gap, and we show it is realizable: one can build a model that matches its safety-aligned base on every static audit yet gives way to a small, known perturbation of its internal state.

At the targeted mid layer the dissociated models score 2.5 to 3.1 times higher LVS than their bases. A bounded latent attack elicits harmful compliance on 54 to 86% of prompts, against 3 to 48% for the bases, while matched random perturbations stay at or below 12%.
Behavioral testing, even with static latent probing, cannot certify representation-level robustness: a safety audit must intervene on the model, not only observe it.
